subject: Money
title: Currency Pegs and Breaks
description: A quick win: understand Currency Pegs and Breaks.

hook.text: In 1992, George Soros bet $10 billion that Britain couldn't hold the pound's peg. He won $1 billion in a day.

buildup.text: Currency pegs fix exchange rates. Central banks must buy or sell their currency to maintain the peg.

discovery.text: Pegs provide stability but require massive reserves. If speculators smell weakness, they attack.

twist.text: Britain spent $6 billion defending the pound before surrendering. Soros proved markets can defeat governments.

climax.text: Currency pegs are a central bank's biggest gamble. Hold it and you control stability. Lose it and you lose billions.

punchline.text: Markets vote with money. They always win.

quiz.question: How much did George Soros profit from breaking the pound?
